prompts: Edit image 1 into the alternate frame of a two-frame pixel-art Inspect animation. Image 1 is the exact master for ALL colours, shading, brightness, silhouette, body proportions, head, torso, left arm, legs, boots, pixel texture and canvas alignment. Image 2 ONLY shows the desired lowered/extended right forearm and magnifying glass pose; DO NOT copy its brighter palette or shifted body. Keep image 1 pixel-for-pixel everywhere except the right forearm/hand/magnifying glass region. Lower and extend that hand and glass slightly toward image 2's pose, using exclusively image 1's existing colours and identical lighting. No global recolouring, no brighter teal or brown, no new highlights, no exposure/contrast adjustment. Preserve image 1's exact head, coat, resting arm, boots, placement, scale and feet baseline. Transparent RGBA background, same canvas dimensions as image 1, single complete sprite, no text, no shadow, no checkerboard. The animation must not flash brightness or change body shape.

Precision palette correction for a two-frame sprite animation. Image 1 is the edit target (alternate frame). Image 2 is the authoritative colour reference (original frame). Keep image 1's exact pose, magnifying glass position, body alignment, dimensions, transparent alpha and all geometry. Correct ONLY its colours to match image 2. In particular boots MUST be darker/less orange: target stable boot midtone approx RGB(120,66,32), not current (129,71,36). Teal coat must be darker/less blue: matching reference stable coat region avg approx RGB(25,82,86), not (29,86,92). These averages describe corresponding patches, not flat fill: preserve the original pixel-art shade structure, but match every corresponding material shade to image 2 including coat teal, trousers, leather brown, skin and hair. No overall relighting, extra highlights, colour grading or shape edits. Copy the reference's actual palette. This is colour calibration to eliminate animation flicker. Exact same 1086x1448 transparent canvas. Output only the corrected alternate frame.
